newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ SPORT - CRICKET - Atherton reiterates he won't resign.
newsitem.headline: NZ SPORT - CRICKET - Atherton reiterates he won't resign.

text.p: AUCKLAND, Jan 6 - The English cricket team have arrived in New Zealand to face yet another barrage from their touring media shortly after landing at Auckland early on Monday morning, NZPA reports.
Touring captain Mike Atherton was again asked whether he would consider resigning his position ahead of the three-test series against New Zealand.
Atherton maintained his position, as previously explained in Zimbabwe, saying he would continue as captain throughout the series.
"The England management have appointed me for the winter series and I intend to see it through.
"I have nothing much more to add to that," Atherton said in reply to a question about whether his team had suffered enough ridicule and embarrassment, and whether he should resign.
Atherton has reiterated his comments made during the tour of Zimbabwe, that he is confident of winning in New Zealand.
"We are confident of beating New Zealand. We played positive cricket in the two tests in Zimbabwe where we felt we had the upper hand," he said.
"Undoubtedly New Zealand are a stronger side (than Zimbabwe) and they've shown that they're continuing to emerge under Lee Germon's captaincy over the last two years."
New Zealand coach Steve Rixon wouldn't take favouritism for the series, but said he hoped his team would quietly achieve what they are setting out to do.
"The team that takes the initiative from day one is the team that is likely to do well.
"We would like to think we will be the quiet achievers," Rixon said.
The English arrival heralded the launch of the New Zealand international season with a car to be presented to the international player of the year at the end of the England and Sri Lanka series.

And in an innovative move, after making a brief reference to Zimbabwean chicken farmer Eddo Brandes, who took five for 28 in the third one-day win by his team against England last week, New Zealand Cricket chief executive Christopher Doig said 100,000 duck callers would be handed out to the public this summer in support of Danny Morrison, whom he dubbed "the duck farmer".
Morrison is having a testimonial season with Auckland. He holds the world record for test ducks and, after having been injured earlier in the season, is expected to play a part in the series.
